chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ الْوَشَّاءِ، عَنْ مُثَنَّى الْحَنَّاطِ، عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abi Basir who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام: تُرَدُّ عَلَيْنَا أَشْيَاءُ لَسْنَا نَعْرِفُهَا فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ وَلَا سُنَّةٍ، فَنَنْظُرُ فِيهَا؟ فَقَالَ: لَا، أَمَا إِنَّكَ إِنْ أَصَبْتَ لَمْ تُؤْجَرْ، وَإِنْ أَخْطَأْتَ كَذَبْتَ عَلَى اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ

translations.en: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Things are referred to us of which we have no knowledge in the Book of Allah nor the Sunnah, should we exercise reason in them?' He said: 'No. Indeed, if you were to get it right, you would not be rewarded, and if you were to err, you would have lied upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

en.summary: Abu Basir asks Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) whether they should use their own reasoning (ijtihad) for matters not explicitly found in the Quran or Sunnah. The Imam replies negatively, stating that if they are correct by chance, they receive no reward, but if they are wrong, they have lied about Allah.
en.seo_question: What is the consequence of using personal reasoning for matters not found in the Quran and Sunnah according to Shia hadith?

key_terms.فَنَنْظُرُ فِيهَا: should we look/exercise reason in them
